question: We upgraded to Doc Detective 5 and leave autoRecord at its default. Our specs don't set runOn. In one test I wrapped the checkout steps in `{ "record": "checkout.mp4" }` and `{ "stopRecord": true }`. Will that stopRecord cut the automatic full-test video short? I'm expecting to get both the full-context video in the run folder and checkout.mp4. And if I leave out the stopRecord step, do I lose the clip?

facts.text: With no runOn, the context runs headless Chrome, and in headless Chrome an explicit `record` step replaces the automatic recording, so that test's context saves only checkout.mp4 and gets no automatic video (no `autoRecording` in its results).
An untargeted `stopRecord` (`true` or `null`) never stops the automatic recording; where both run, Doc Detective finalizes the automatic recording at the end of the context.
Without a `stopRecord` step, Doc Detective stops and saves any recording still running when the test (context) ends, so the clip isn't lost.

must_not: The `stopRecord: true` step stops, or cuts short, the automatic full-context recording.
The default headless Chrome context produces both the automatic full-context video and checkout.mp4.
Without a `stopRecord` step the recording is discarded, not saved, or the test fails.

wrong.why: says both videos come out and stopRecord ends the auto video
wrong.answer: Yes, it will. `stopRecord: true` stops the most recent recording, and the automatic recording counts, so it can end the full-context video early. Give your clip a name and stop it by name instead: `{ "record": { "path": "checkout.mp4", "name": "checkout" } }` and `{ "stopRecord": "checkout" }`. You then get both videos: the automatic full-context video in the run folder and checkout.mp4. Always keep the stopRecord step, because a recording that's never stopped is discarded.

replace.from:
In this test, though, there's no automatic recording to cut short. A context with no `runOn` runs headless Chrome. In headless Chrome, an explicit `record` step replaces the automatic recording, because a Chrome context records one tab at a time. So that context saves `checkout.mp4` only, and its results have no `autoRecording` field. Your other tests, with no `record` step, still get the automatic video at `.doc-detective/runs/<runId>/specs/<specId>/tests/<testId>/contexts/<contextId>/recordings/<contextId>.mp4`.

To get both videos from one test, run it headed (`headless: false` on the browser in `runOn`). The automatic recording then captures the screen with the `ffmpeg` engine, and your `record` step records the tab with the `browser` engine. A headed context needs a display, or Xvfb on Linux.
